appendBlocks.title: Level-up → the full UC hierarchy
appendBlocks.text: Metastore → catalog → schema → object, managed vs external storage, and why UC governs metadata but never stores the bytes are now covered in depth — see Chapter 11: Unity Catalog Mastery.

appendBlocks.title: Level-up → principals in production
appendBlocks.text: New: provision principals at the **account level**, and give **production ownership and write access** to groups / service principals, never personal users — see Chapter 11: Unity Catalog Mastery.

appendBlocks.title: Level-up → inheritance, REVOKE, ownership, MANAGE, BROWSE
appendBlocks.text: Grants on a schema/catalog **flow down** to children (including future tables), so a table-level `REVOKE` can leave access in place. Ownership, MANAGE, BROWSE and SHOW GRANTS are covered too — see Chapter 11: Unity Catalog Mastery.

appendExercises.q: After `REVOKE SELECT ON TABLE company.finance.transactions FROM analysts`, analysts are guaranteed to lose read access to that table.
appendExercises.explain: False. If `SELECT` was also granted on the parent **schema** or **catalog**, the table inherits it and access remains. Always run SHOW GRANTS on the schema and catalog too (Chapter 11, Case 3).

appendPitfalls.title: REVOKE on a table ≠ access gone
appendPitfalls.text: Inherited SELECT on the schema or catalog keeps the table readable after a table-level REVOKE.
appendPitfalls.fix: SHOW GRANTS on schema and catalog; restructure where SELECT is granted.

appendFlashcards.q: Why can a user still read a table after REVOKE SELECT ON TABLE?
appendFlashcards.a: An inherited SELECT on the parent schema or catalog.

appendBlocks.title: Level-up → the 8-layer PERMISSION_DENIED algorithm
appendBlocks.text: The full algorithm puts **identity first** and adds three layers this checklist lacks: **workspace binding**, **external storage** (location / credential / cloud IAM) and **UC-compatible compute**. Mnemonic: *I Bet Cats Sit On Fluffy Silk Cushions* — see Chapter 11: Unity Catalog Mastery.

appendExercises.q: The Phase-3 permission algorithm extends this section's checklist. Which layers does it ADD? (choose all)
options: External-storage permissions (external location, credential, cloud IAM)
why: Added — grants can't override a missing binding.
Added — correct grants on legacy compute still fail.
appendExercises.explain: Full order: Identity → Binding → USE CATALOG → USE SCHEMA → Object → Fine-grained → Storage → Compute. Binding, storage and compute are the new layers; identity also moves to the front, because every grant is evaluated for the executing principal.

appendExercises.q: Put the 8 layers of the full PERMISSION_DENIED algorithm in order.
appendExercises.explain: I Bet Cats Sit On Fluffy Silk Cushions: Identity, Binding, Catalog, Schema, Object, Fine-grained, Storage, Compute.

appendFlashcards.a: I Bet Cats Sit On Fluffy Silk Cushions — Identity, Binding, Catalog, Schema, Object, Fine-grained, Storage, Compute.

appendBlocks.title: Level-up → ALL PRIVILEGES is not everything
appendBlocks.text: `ALL PRIVILEGES` **excludes MANAGE, EXTERNAL USE LOCATION and EXTERNAL USE SCHEMA**, and it is **evaluated dynamically** (new privileges are added automatically) — one more reason for restraint — see Chapter 11: Unity Catalog Mastery.

appendExercises.q: `ALL PRIVILEGES` is a fixed list that includes MANAGE.
appendExercises.explain: False twice: MANAGE (plus EXTERNAL USE LOCATION / EXTERNAL USE SCHEMA) is excluded, and ALL PRIVILEGES is evaluated dynamically, so it silently grows when new applicable privileges appear.

appendFlashcards.a: MANAGE, EXTERNAL USE LOCATION, EXTERNAL USE SCHEMA.

appendBlocks.title: Level-up → workspace ≠ metastore
appendBlocks.text: Usually **one metastore per region**; many workspaces attach to it and share governance. A notebook lives in a workspace, but `prod.sales.orders` is registered in the metastore — see Chapter 11: Unity Catalog Mastery.

appendExercises.q: A table created from workspace A can be queried from workspace B in the same region, if both use the same metastore, the principal has the grants and no workspace binding blocks it.
appendExercises.explain: True. Tables are registered in the regional **metastore**, not in a workspace. Same metastore + grants + no blocking binding = access from any attached workspace.

appendFlashcards.q: Typical number of UC metastores per region?
appendFlashcards.a: One, shared by the region's workspaces.

appendBlocks.title: Level-up → Catalog Explorer as governance UI
appendBlocks.text: Per object you can see schema, details, **permissions, history, lineage, tags, dependencies**; BROWSE lets users discover objects without data access — see Chapter 11: Unity Catalog Mastery.

appendBlocks.title: Level-up → catalog.schema.object
appendBlocks.text: The third name can be a table, view, **volume, function, model**, materialized view or streaming table — so the general form is `catalog.schema.object`. Catalog/schema design and creation privileges are covered — see Chapter 11: Unity Catalog Mastery.

appendBlocks.title: Level-up → six permission-debugging cases
appendBlocks.text: Wrong identity, SELECT without USE SCHEMA, revoked-but-inherited, external-storage failures, volume READ/WRITE VOLUME and masked values each get a playbook — see Chapter 11: Unity Catalog Mastery.

appendBlocks.title: Level-up → access mode = UC compatibility
appendBlocks.text: Classic compute in **Standard or Dedicated** access mode, serverless and Databricks SQL can access Unity Catalog. **Correct permissions + wrong legacy compute = still failure** — see Chapter 11: Unity Catalog Mastery.

appendExercises.q: If a user's Unity Catalog grants are correct, the query works on any cluster, whatever its configuration.
appendExercises.explain: False. The compute must be UC-compatible (Standard/Dedicated classic, serverless, SQL warehouse). A legacy configuration fails even with perfect grants — layer 8 of the permission algorithm.

appendFlashcards.q: Which compute can access Unity Catalog?
appendFlashcards.a: Classic Standard/Dedicated access mode, serverless, Databricks SQL.

appendBlocks.title: Level-up → what Gate 2 really contains
appendBlocks.text: "Unity Catalog" in Gate 2 is itself a chain: workspace binding → USE CATALOG → USE SCHEMA → object privilege → row filters / masks / ABAC → external storage — see Chapter 11: Unity Catalog Mastery.

appendBlocks.title: Level-up → run-as = Case 1
appendBlocks.text: "Notebook works, job/pipeline fails" is Debugging Case 1 (wrong identity). The production example `gold_pipeline_sp` gets read-Silver + write-Gold grants only — see Chapter 11: Unity Catalog Mastery.
